title: Israeli military orders evacuation of Kiryat Shmona amid escalating fire from Lebanon
body:
On 20 October 2023 the Israeli military ordered the evacuation of the northern city of Kiryat Shmona, which had about 22,000 residents, many of whom had already left, according to The Times of Israel. The order came amid escalating exchanges of fire with Hezbollah and other armed groups in Lebanon, in the second week of the war that followed the Hamas attack of 7 October.

The Defense Ministry's National Emergency Management Authority had also begun evacuating all communities within two kilometres of the Lebanese border, covering 28 towns and villages with an estimated 27,000 residents. On Thursday 19 October a rocket hit a home in Kiryat Shmona and wounded three residents, which the newspaper described as apparently the gravest attack on the city since 2006. On 20 October a reservist was seriously wounded in a shooting near Margaliot, and the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said it struck five cells in southern Lebanon. Some 20 to 30 rockets were fired at the Mount Dov area and two landed near Metula, with no injuries; Hezbollah claimed responsibility for rockets and gunfire.

The Times of Israel reported that at least five Israeli soldiers, one Israeli civilian, 13 Hezbollah operatives and five Palestinian militants had been killed in the border exchanges up to that point, and that several Lebanese civilians and a journalist were reported killed by Israeli shelling. IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Herzi Halevi had said on 17 October that if Hezbollah made a mistake it would face destruction. The evacuations were the first of the northern Israeli communities that remained displaced for much of the following year.
